tools.name: search_worksites
tools.description: Find worksites by name, with optional state, city or NAICS industry code. Results are ordered by name match, then by name, never by rate. Returns name, address, industry, site_id and the latest year reported.

tools.name: get_worksite
tools.description: The injury summary a worksite filed with OSHA for each year, the computed rates, the range, the BLS national rate and the comparison, with caveats and sources.

tools.name: get_employer
tools.description: Totals across the worksites that filed under one employer tax ID, by year, how many worksites the totals are based on, and the first 50 worksites by name.

tools.name: get_parent_company
tools.description: Returns a parent company and the employers linked to it, with the public record that proves each link. The record is either a GLEIF relationship record, where parent_id is an LEI, or the parent's SEC Exhibit 21 subsidiary list, where parent_id is a 10-digit SEC CIK. By name, it returns up to 25 pare

tools.name: compare_worksites
tools.description: The tool puts two to four worksites side by side. It shows the latest figures filed with OSHA, the three-year rate with its range, and the BLS national rate. It lists worksites in the order given, never by rate. When two ranges overlap, the answer says the figures do not show a difference.

tools.name: get_industry_benchmark
tools.description: The BLS national injury rate for a NAICS industry code, by year and by establishment size class, with quartiles where BLS publishes them.

tools.name: list_industries
tools.description: The tool lists NAICS industry codes with an industry page, the industry name, and the number of worksites with a page. You can filter by a word in the name or by the start of the code. The tool returns at most 50 rows in code order.

tools.name: find_contractors
tools.description: The tool lists worksites in one state and one NAICS trade code in name order, never by rate. It shows each worksite's three-year rate, range, and hours. You can use the list to build a shortlist for vetting, then read each worksite's own record.

tools.name: get_inspections
tools.description: OSHA lists inspections opened since 2012 for one worksite or by year across one employer's worksites. For one worksite, the tool returns the latest 25 inspections with totals. tools.description: OSHA severe injury reports cover in-patient hospitalization, amputation, and loss of an eye. The tool counts reports by year for one worksite or sums them across one employer's worksites. It covers Federal OSHA states only, from 2015 to November 2025. tools.description: Search MSHA's open government data by mine name, operator name or controller name, or by exact MSHA mine ID, optionally in one state. tools.description: Get one mine's record from MSHA open government data by year since 2016. tools.description: Get one mine controller's record from MSHA open government data. The record sums hours, injuries as reported to MSHA, violations and penalties by year across the mines it held for the most days of each year. tools.name: search_railroads
tools.description: Search the Federal Railroad Administration's casualty data (Form FRA F 6180.55a) by railroad name, FRA code or parent railroad name. The tool returns each railroad's FRA code, name, parent railroad and the first and last year in FRA's file. It orders results by name match, then name, then FRA code,

tools.name: get_railroad
tools.description: Get one railroad's record from the Federal Railroad Administration's casualty data by FRA code. tools.name: search_offshore_operators
tools.description: Search the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement's offshore incident files by operator name. The tool returns each operator's ID, name as BSEE writes it, and the first and last year in BSEE's files. It orders results by name match, then name, never by a count.

tools.name: get_offshore_operator
tools.description: Get one offshore oil and gas operator's record from the Bureau of Safety and Environmental Enforcement's incident files by operator ID. tools.name: get_coverage
tools.description: The tool shows who must report to OSHA, how many worksites filed, and how that compares with all establishments in the Census County Business Patterns count, nationally or for one state. With a NAICS code, it also shows the number of worksites with a page in that industry.

tools.name: get_data_sources
tools.description: The public files behind the figures, when each was fetched, and where the method is described.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "compare_worksites" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.detail: Description of "compare_worksites" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "get_railroad" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.
